text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The government has worked out a package of unspecified measures to help curb the widening foreign trade deficit.
- Overall volume of Slovak investment abroad totalled 1.7 billion crown in 1996.
- Deutsche Bank Research predicts a gradual depreciation of the crown in coming months.

- The President of Russian gas producer Gazprom, Rem Vyachirev, has said Slovakia was offering unacceptable goods as payment for gas deliveries agreed upon in the recently signed Russian-Slovak gas transport joint-venture.
- The government is aware of the fact that it has to adopt some changes to the state budget, Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said.
- Local money market dealers expect interbank rates to range between 20 to 25 percent in the coming days.
- Traders said the eight largest market players should meet in the near future to discuss the current situation on the money market.
SME - Five main opposition parties, except the Party of the Democratic Left (SDL), are expected to sign the creation of a pre-election coalition in the near future.
- Jan Carnogursky, chairman of the strongest opposition party, the Christian Democratic Movement (KDH), said he would try to become the leader of the new opposition coalition.
PRAVDA - The opposition coalition said it planned to gain some 40 percent in the next parliamentary elections scheduled for 1998.
- The SDL said it would accept Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's invitation to round table discussions without setting any conditions before the talks.
- The association of agricultural firms demands 4,300 crowns per a tonne of grain from this year's harvest.
PRACA - Slovakia's sole aluminium producer ZSNP Ziar Nad Hronom said it planned to post a profit of some 560 million crowns this year, compared with a loss of 2.3 million crowns in 1996.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The law on the Slovak Export-Import bank becomes effective on July 1, 1997.
